cohort: 120 women who underwent cesarean section following a failed vacuum extraction and 551 women who underwent cesarean section in the second stage of labor without a vacuum extraction attempt, at a single tertiary university-affiliated medical center between 2012-2019
finding: Failed vacuum extraction before cesarean section in the second stage of labor is associated with increased neonatal morbidity, but not increased maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: Failed vacuum attempt is associated with a significant increased neonatal morbidity, but not increased maternal morbidity.
